gitCommit.subject: Cover the remaining failure paths, drop a duplicated dead method
gitCommit.body:
Cover the remaining failure paths, drop a duplicated dead method

CI coverage came back at 77.23% against a 77.74% floor with 0.5 tolerance —
short of the 77.24% threshold by roughly one line. Rather than chase the number,
close the real gaps left in the code this PR touches.

ImportFinalizer goes to fully covered. Everything after the import is a
post-processing step, and none of them is a reason to lose a statement whose rows
are already written, so each failure is logged and swallowed — four specs assert
the swallowing actually happens for the investment classifier, the excluded-pair
marker, transfer reconciliation, and a push notification that cannot be enqueued.

Removed `no_transactions?` from the concern: Statements::Processor defines its own
and is the only caller, so the copy in ImportFinalizer had no path to it. Its five
branches are now covered where they actually live, through Processor — including
the one that matters most, a StatementFile payload meaning the rows already
imported and vision must not run again over a statement that succeeded.

CategoryRules::Creator's two untested paths are covered too: an unsaveable record
surfacing its errors, and the RecordNotUnique recovery. Statement imports fan out
across Sidekiq workers, so two really can correct the same description at once and
the loser of that race has to adopt the winner's rule rather than raise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
